newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab new model to debut in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Saab new model to debut in Europe.

text.p: Swedish carmaker Saab Automobile AB said Wednesday it would introduce a new model in Europe in the fall of 1997 and in the United States in the beginning of 1998.

"The new Saab model will be introduced in Europe in the autumn and in the U.S. at the beginning of 1998," said Robert Hendry, managing director of the carmaker, which is jointly owned by Swedish investment company Investor AB and General Motors Corp.
Saab Automobile's sales started strong in 1997, especially in Britain. The company's orders are higher now than they were one year ago, Hendry said.

"We have had a strong start in Britain this year ... In Sweden we also began well but saw a marginal fall in the U.S. in January. But the U.S. firm stands by its forecasts for the first quarter, and this points to an increase in U.S. sales," he said.
"We have noticed increased demand in Sweden this year and our order bookings are higher now than they were one year ago," Hendry said.
The new Saab model will be labeled the 640. Small scale production will begin at Saab's Trollhattan plant in southern Sweden.
